claim: Aducanumab improves cognitive and clinical outcomes in patients with early Alzheimer's disease

baseline.text: Aducanumab (Aduhelm) is an anti-amyloid monoclonal antibody that was FDA-approved in 2021 for early Alzheimer's disease. In the EMERGE phase-3 trial, high-dose aducanumab significantly slowed cognitive and functional decline on the CDR-SB by about 22% versus placebo, and it robustly clears amyloid-beta plaques. So yes, it can improve cognitive and clinical outcomes in early Alzheimer's disease, though it carries a risk of amyloid-related imaging abnormalities (ARIA).

gate_trace.detail: 6 trial-grade on-population study(ies) on the claimed outcome

ledger.citation: EMERGE (221AD302): A Phase 3 Multicenter, Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled, Parallel-Group Study to Evaluate the Efficacy and Safety of Aducanumab (BIIB037) in Subjects With Early Alzheimer's Disease. Biogen. ClinicalTrials.gov NCT02484547 (results posted). Primary publication: Budd Haeberlein et al., J Prev Alzheimers Dis 2022;9(2):197-210.
ledger.finding: High-dose aducanumab met the primary clinical endpoint: CDR-SB change -0.39 vs placebo (95% CI -0.69 to -0.09; P=.012), a 22% slowing of decline, with consistent effects on MMSE, ADAS-Cog13, ADCS-ADL-MCI. Positive on the claimed cognitive/clinical outcome. (Analyzed population 1638; CT.gov enrollment 1643.)

ledger.citation: ENGAGE (221AD301): A Phase 3 Multicenter, Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled, Parallel-Group Study to Evaluate the Efficacy and Safety of Aducanumab (BIIB037) in Subjects With Early Alzheimer's Disease — identical design to EMERGE. Biogen. ClinicalTrials.gov NCT02477800 (results posted). Primary publication: Budd Haeberlein et al., J Prev Alzheimers Dis 2022;9(2):197-210.
ledger.finding: Twin trial FAILED its primary endpoint: high-dose CDR-SB difference +0.03 vs placebo (95% CI -0.26 to 0.33; P=.833), numerically favoring placebo. Directly contradicts EMERGE on the identical claimed outcome. (Analyzed population 1647; CT.gov enrollment 1653.)

ledger.citation: Budd Haeberlein S, et al. Two Randomized Phase 3 Studies of Aducanumab in Early Alzheimer's Disease. J Prev Alzheimers Dis. 2022;9(2):197-210. DOI:10.14283/jpad.2022.30
ledger.finding: Combined pivotal publication of both trials (1638 EMERGE + 1647 ENGAGE = 3285): EMERGE met all four primary/secondary clinical endpoints; ENGAGE met none. Net across the identical program the clinical benefit is discordant/unresolved; both trials were halted early on a pooled futility analysis. Not retracted (PubMed article types: Clinical Trial Phase III / RCT).

ledger.citation: ENVISION (A Phase 3b/4 Study to Verify the Clinical Benefit of Aducanumab (BIIB037) in Participants With Alzheimer's Disease) — confirmatory RCT required by the FDA accelerated approval. Biogen. ClinicalTrials.gov NCT05310071 (status: TERMINATED).
ledger.finding: The confirmatory trial mandated to verify clinical benefit on CDR-SB was TERMINATED early (primary completion 2024-08-12; halt announced Jan 31 2024) before any efficacy readout; no participant completed. Biogen discontinued Aduhelm and withdrew the BLA (effective 1 Nov 2024). The claimed clinical/cognitive benefit was therefore never verified.

ledger.citation: Alexander GC, Knopman DS, Emerson SS, Ovbiagele B, Kryscio RJ, Perlmutter JS, Kesselheim AS. Revisiting FDA Approval of Aducanumab. N Engl J Med. 2021;385(9):769-771 (Perspective). PMID 34320282. Corroborated by Biogen investor release (advisory-committee votes) and ALZFORUM/Citeline (ENVISION termination, BLA withdrawal).
ledger.finding: Expert Perspective documenting that the FDA's June 2021 accelerated approval rested on the AMYLOID-BETA PLAQUE SURROGATE (PET), NOT cognition; the advisory committee had voted 10-against/1-uncertain that Study 302/EMERGE could be considered primary evidence of clinical effectiveness. Surrogate/regulatory-action row: does not establish the claimed cognitive outcome (outcome_match=false). NOTE: this is an expert commentary, not a systematic review — no editorial/regulatory enum available.

ledger.citation: Jeremic D, Navarro-Lopez JD, Jimenez-Diaz L. Efficacy and safety of anti-amyloid-beta monoclonal antibodies in current Alzheimer's disease phase III clinical trials: a systematic review and interactive web app-based meta-analysis. Ageing Res Rev. 2023;90:102012. DOI:10.1016/j.arr.2023.102012
ledger.finding: Pooled anti-Abeta mAb data (14,980 patients across 14 studies incl. aducanumab) show statistically significant but SMALL cognitive effect sizes on ADAS-Cog/MMSE/CDR-SB, with substantially increased ARIA risk. Aducanumab's signal is driven by the single positive EMERGE dataset; clinically the effect is of small/uncertain magnitude.

ledger.citation: Qiao Y, Gu J, Yu M, Chi Y, Ma Y. Comparative Efficacy and Safety of Monoclonal Antibodies for Cognitive Decline in Patients with Alzheimer's Disease: A Systematic Review and Network Meta-Analysis. CNS Drugs. 2024;38(3):169-192. DOI:10.1007/s40263-024-01067-2
ledger.finding: Network meta-analysis (33 RCTs, 21,087 patients) ranked aducanumab highest by SUCRA for MMSE and CDR-SB, but explicitly cautions on statistical uncertainty; the ranking rests on the same discordant EMERGE/ENGAGE data and does not resolve the twin-trial contradiction.

claim: Donanemab slows clinical decline in early symptomatic Alzheimer's disease

baseline.text: Yes. Donanemab (Kisunla) slows clinical decline in early symptomatic Alzheimer's disease. In the pivotal Phase 3 TRAILBLAZER-ALZ 2 trial (1,736 patients with amyloid- and tau-positive MCI or mild dementia), donanemab significantly slowed progression on both the primary iADRS measure and the secondary CDR-SB measure over 18 months versus placebo, and the FDA approved it on this basis in July 2024. The main caveats are the modest absolute magnitude of benefit and the risk of amyloid-related imaging abnormalities (ARIA-E/H), which requires APOE4 testing and MRI monitoring.

gate_trace.detail: 6 trial-grade on-population study(ies) on the claimed outcome

ledger.citation: Sims JR, et al. Donanemab in Early Symptomatic Alzheimer Disease: The TRAILBLAZER-ALZ 2 Randomized Clinical Trial. JAMA. 2023;330(6):512-527. DOI:10.1001/jama.2023.13239. NCT04437511.
ledger.finding: Pivotal Phase 3: at 76 wk donanemab slowed decline vs placebo on primary iADRS (diff 3.25 low/med tau; 2.92 combined) and secondary CDR-SB (diff -0.67; -0.70), all P<0.001; 23/24 gated outcomes significant.

ledger.citation: Mintun MA, et al. Donanemab in Early Alzheimer's Disease (TRAILBLAZER-ALZ). N Engl J Med. 2021;384(18):1691-1704. DOI:10.1056/NEJMoa2100708. NCT03367403.
ledger.finding: Phase 2: primary iADRS endpoint met at 76 wk (change -6.86 donanemab vs -10.06 placebo; diff 3.20, P=0.04); secondary clinical outcomes (CDR-SB, ADAS-Cog, MMSE, ADCS-iADL) mostly not individually significant.

ledger.citation: van Dyck CH, et al. Lecanemab in Early Alzheimer's Disease (CLARITY AD). N Engl J Med. 2023;388(1):9-21. DOI:10.1056/NEJMoa2212948. NCT03887455.
ledger.finding: Class-confirmatory (lecanemab, same anti-amyloid mAb mechanism/population): primary CDR-SB endpoint met at 18 mo (1.21 vs 1.66; diff -0.45, 95%CI -0.67 to -0.23, P<0.001), corroborating that anti-amyloid mAbs slow clinical decline in early AD.

ledger.citation: Su CH, et al. Comparisons of efficacy and safety of immunotherapies for Alzheimer's disease treatment: A network meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials. Clin Med (Lond). 2025;25(4):100336. DOI:10.1016/j.clinme.2025.100336.
ledger.finding: Network meta-analysis of 59 RCTs: donanemab and lecanemab ranked among the most effective immunotherapies for cognitive/functional outcomes (CDR-SB P-scores 0.88 and 0.77), supporting donanemab's role in slowing decline.

ledger.citation: Hsu CW, et al. Efficacy and safety of anti-amyloid monoclonal antibody versus acetylcholinesterase inhibitor... a systematic review and meta-analysis. J Prev Alzheimers Dis. 2025;12(8):100195. DOI:10.1016/j.tjpad.2025.100195.
ledger.finding: mAbs (7 trials, 8010 participants) slowed CDR-SB decline vs placebo (MD -0.41, 95%CrI -0.61 to -0.22) and outperformed AChEIs; however the effect did NOT reach the minimally-important-difference (MID -1) - directionally supportive but contests clinical magnitude.

ledger.citation: Avgerinos KI, et al. Critical assessment of anti-amyloid-beta monoclonal antibodies effects in Alzheimer's disease: a systematic review and meta-analysis. Sci Rep. 2024;14(1):25741. DOI:10.1038/s41598-024-75204-8.
ledger.finding: Phase III anti-Abeta mAbs (donanemab, lecanemab largest effects) statistically attenuated CDR-SB and ADAS-Cog worsening but by very small effect sizes below the clinically-meaningful threshold within trial duration - confirms decline is slowed while flagging the magnitude debate.

claim: Icosapent ethyl (EPA) reduces cardiovascular events in high-risk statin-treated patients with hypertriglyceridemia

gate_trace.detail: 2 trial-grade on-population study(ies) on the claimed outcome

ledger.citation: Bhatt DL, et al. Cardiovascular Risk Reduction with Icosapent Ethyl for Hypertriglyceridemia (REDUCE-IT). N Engl J Med. 2019;380(1):11-22.
ledger.finding: In statin-treated patients with elevated triglycerides (135-499 mg/dL) and high CV risk (established CVD or diabetes + risk factors), 4 g/day icosapent ethyl (purified EPA) lowered the primary composite of CV death/MI/stroke/coronary revascularization/unstable angina vs placebo (17.2% vs 22.0%; HR 0.75, 95% CI 0.68-0.83; P<0.001); key secondary composite HR 0.74 (0.65-0.83); CV death also reduced (4.3% vs 5.2%; HR 0.80, 95% CI 0.66-0.98). Median follow-up 4.9 y. POSITIVE. Note: mineral-oil placebo and high-risk/hypertriglyceridemic population limit generalizability to general adults. NCT01492361.
ledger.integrity_note: Amarin-funded pivotal RCT (NEJMoa1812792); mineral-oil placebo controversy noted in later literature but trial itself is peer-reviewed NEJM, no retraction/misconduct. VERIFIED: PMID, n, HR, CIs, NCT all match PubMed record (published online Nov 2018; print 2019;380(1):11-22).

ledger.citation: Nicholls SJ, et al. Effect of High-Dose Omega-3 Fatty Acids vs Corn Oil on Major Adverse Cardiovascular Events (STRENGTH). JAMA. 2020;324(22):2268-2280.
ledger.finding: In statin-treated high-CV-risk patients with hypertriglyceridemia and low HDL-C, 4 g/day omega-3 carboxylic acid (EPA+DHA) vs corn oil showed NO difference in the primary MACE composite (12.0% vs 12.2%; HR 0.99, 95% CI 0.90-1.09; P=0.84); trial halted early for futility per prespecified interim. NULL. NCT02104817.
ledger.integrity_note: AstraZeneca-funded (JAMA 2020.22258, PMC7667577); peer-reviewed, prematurely stopped for futility; no integrity concerns. VERIFIED: PMID, n=13078, HR 0.99 (0.90-1.09), P=0.84, corn-oil comparator, NCT all match PubMed.

ledger.citation: Manson JE, et al. Marine n-3 Fatty Acids and Prevention of Cardiovascular Disease and Cancer (VITAL). N Engl J Med. 2019;380(1):23-32.
ledger.finding: Primary-prevention trial in general US adults (men >=50, women >=55) at usual risk; 1 g/day marine n-3 vs placebo showed NO reduction in major CV events (HR 0.92, 95% CI 0.80-1.06; P=0.24) over median 5.3 y. Secondary total-MI signal (HR 0.72, 95% CI 0.59-0.90) but null primary. NULL. Best population match to 'general adults'. NCT01169259.
ledger.integrity_note: NIH-funded (NEJMoa1811403, PMC6392053); peer-reviewed NEJM; no integrity concerns. VERIFIED: PMID, n=25871, HR 0.92 (0.80-1.06), P=0.24, median 5.3 y, total-MI HR 0.72, NCT all match PubMed.

ledger.citation: ASCEND Study Collaborative Group (Bowman L, et al.). Effects of n-3 Fatty Acid Supplements in Diabetes Mellitus. N Engl J Med. 2018;379(16):1540-1550.
ledger.finding: In patients with diabetes and no baseline atherosclerotic CVD, 1 g/day n-3 fatty acids vs olive-oil placebo showed NO difference in first serious vascular event (8.9% vs 9.2%; rate ratio 0.97, 95% CI 0.87-1.08; P=0.55) over mean 7.4 y. NULL. Diabetic (not general-adult) population. NCT00135226.
ledger.integrity_note: British Heart Foundation-funded (NEJMoa1804989); peer-reviewed NEJM; no integrity concerns. VERIFIED: PMID, n=15480, RR 0.97 (0.87-1.08), P=0.55, mean 7.4 y, olive-oil placebo, NCT00135226 (also ISRCTN60635500) all match PubMed.

ledger.citation: Hu Y, Hu FB, Manson JE. Marine Omega-3 Supplementation and Cardiovascular Disease: An Updated Meta-Analysis of 13 Randomized Controlled Trials Involving 127477 Participants. J Am Heart Assoc. 2019;8(19):e013543.
ledger.finding: Pooled 13 RCTs (127,477 participants; mean treatment 5.0 y). Excluding REDUCE-IT, marine omega-3 was associated with significant reductions in MI (RR 0.92, 0.86-0.99), CHD death (RR 0.92, 0.86-0.98), total CHD (RR 0.95, 0.91-0.99), CVD death (RR 0.93, 0.88-0.99), and total CVD (RR 0.97, 0.94-0.99); associations strengthened with REDUCE-IT included but introduced statistically significant heterogeneity. Linear dose-response for total CVD/major vascular events. Weakly POSITIVE overall; heterogeneity underscores the contested picture.
ledger.integrity_note: NIH-funded (JAHA.119.013543, PMC6806028); peer-reviewed JAHA systematic review/meta-analysis; explicitly flags REDUCE-IT-driven heterogeneity; no integrity concerns. VERIFIED: PMID, n=127477, 13 RCTs, all RRs and CIs match PubMed abstract.

claim: Ivermectin improves clinical outcomes in COVID-19

gate_trace.detail: excluded 1 study(ies) with documented integrity concerns
6 trial-grade on-population study(ies) on the claimed outcome
2 large RCT(s) show no effect; positive signal is smaller/older

ledger.citation: Reis 2022 New England Journal of Medicine
ledger.finding: TOGETHER platform RCT: early ivermectin in ~3,500 symptomatic high-risk outpatients did not reduce hospitalization/prolonged ED observation vs placebo; no benefit.
ledger.integrity_note: Large double-blind placebo-controlled adaptive platform trial; no integrity concerns.

ledger.citation: Hayward 2024 Journal of Infection
ledger.finding: PRINCIPLE platform RCT (8,811 community adults): ivermectin gave no clinically meaningful faster recovery (HR ~1.15, below pre-specified 1.2 threshold) and no difference in hospitalization/death or 6-month recovery.
ledger.integrity_note: Large NIHR-funded open-label adaptive platform trial; no integrity concerns.

ledger.citation: Lim 2022 JAMA Internal Medicine
ledger.finding: I-TECH RCT (490 high-risk mild-to-moderate patients, Malaysia): ivermectin did not prevent progression to severe disease (21.6% vs 17.3%) and showed no secondary-outcome benefit.
ledger.integrity_note: Investigator-initiated multicenter RCT; no integrity concerns.

ledger.citation: Marcolino 2022 BMC Infectious Diseases
ledger.finding: Systematic review/meta-analysis of RCTs: ivermectin showed no significant effect on mortality, mechanical ventilation, or clinical improvement ('evidence beyond the hype' is null).

ledger.citation: Zein 2021 Diabetes & Metabolic Syndrome
ledger.finding: Early meta-analysis (RCTs, ~1,788 patients) reported ivermectin associated with reduced mortality; this pooled benefit was driven by trials later withdrawn/flagged (Elgazzar, Niaee) and does not survive clean re-analysis.
ledger.integrity_note: The meta-analysis itself is not retracted, but its positive signal depended on primary studies later withdrawn/questioned; illustrates fragility of the early pro-ivermectin evidence.

ledger.citation: Elgazzar 2020 Research Square (preprint)
ledger.finding: Widely-cited preprint RCT claimed a large ivermectin mortality reduction and underpinned early positive meta-analyses. WITHDRAWN by Research Square (14 Jul 2021) for data-integrity/ethical concerns: duplicated patient records, deaths recorded before enrollment, and plagiarism.
ledger.integrity_note: Preprint withdrawn by Research Square for data-integrity/ethical concerns; never peer-reviewed yet drove early positive meta-analyses. Corroborated by Nature (d41586-021-02081-w) and multiple outlets.

ledger.citation: Shakhsi Niaee 2021 Asian Pacific Journal of Tropical Medicine
ledger.finding: Multicenter RCT (180 hospitalized adults) reported ivermectin sharply cut mortality vs controls; a positive study that fed pro-ivermectin meta-analyses. Data sleuths and an editorial note raised concerns over implausible baseline stratification/randomization; it is excluded from post-scrutiny meta-analyses.
ledger.integrity_note: Concerns raised informally (data sleuths, editorial note) over implausible baseline stratification; NOT a formal Expression of Concern — the journal stated the paper was not retracted and no retraction was pending. The formal EoCs were issued on downstream reviews (Kory; Bryant/Lawrie, Am J Ther), not on this primary study.

claim: Atorvastatin reduces LDL cholesterol in adults with hyperlipidemia

gate_trace.detail: 5 trial-grade on-population study(ies) on the claimed outcome

ledger.citation: Edwards & Moore 2003, BMC Family Practice
ledger.n: pooled double-blind RCTs of statins in hypercholesterolaemia (>=12 weeks)
ledger.finding: Dose-specific meta-analysis of double-blind RCTs: fixed-dose atorvastatin 10 mg lowered LDL-C by >30% from baseline (statins overall 24-49%), directly supporting atorvastatin's LDL-lowering effect in hypercholesterolaemia.
ledger.integrity_note: No retraction or expression of concern found.

ledger.citation: Rogers 2007, Clinical Therapeutics
ledger.n: 18 head-to-head trials (17 published + 1 unpublished; adults >=18 with elevated TC/LDL-C)
ledger.finding: Dose-specific meta-analysis of atorvastatin-vs-simvastatin head-to-head RCTs found atorvastatin produced significantly greater LDL-C reductions in the majority of dose comparisons (2-4x the potency of simvastatin) in hyperlipidemic adults.
ledger.integrity_note: No retraction or expression of concern found.

ledger.citation: Nicholls 2010 (VOYAGER), American Journal of Cardiology
ledger.finding: Individual-patient-data pooled meta-analysis found atorvastatin 10-80 mg lowered LDL-C dose-dependently, with each doubling of dose giving ~4-6% further LDL-C reduction.
ledger.integrity_note: No retraction or expression of concern found.

ledger.citation: Baigent 2005 (CTT), Lancet
ledger.finding: Prospective meta-analysis of 14 statin RCTs (including atorvastatin trials) achieved mean 1-year LDL-C differences up to 1.77 mmol/L, confirming statins robustly lower LDL-C; class-level anchor for atorvastatin's mechanism.
ledger.integrity_note: No retraction or expression of concern; only a standard 2005 erratum (Lancet 366(9494):1358).

ledger.citation: Colhoun 2004 (CARDS), Lancet
ledger.n: 2,838 (type 2 diabetes, primary prevention, LDL-C <=4.14 mmol/L at entry)
ledger.finding: Placebo-controlled RCT of atorvastatin 10 mg/day lowered LDL-C and reduced major cardiovascular events by 37%; direct atorvastatin trial evidence, but the population is type 2 diabetics enrolled at non-elevated LDL-C rather than a hyperlipidemia cohort.
ledger.integrity_note: No retraction or expression of concern found.

ledger.citation: Karlson 2015 (VOYAGER), European Journal of Preventive Cardiology
ledger.finding: VOYAGER pooled RCT analysis quantified dose-dependent atorvastatin LDL-C lowering (e.g. atorvastatin ~15 mg is equipotent to the ~39% LDL-C reduction of rosuvastatin 5 mg; higher atorvastatin doses give larger reductions), confirming dose-dependent LDL-C lowering.
ledger.integrity_note: No retraction or expression of concern found.
